Topographic Position Index

tpi.Rd

Calculates the Topographic Position Index (TPI), that is the difference between the elevation of each cell and the mean elevation of its neighbourhood (Guisan et al. 1999; Weiss 2001), optionally standardised. This is the quantity on which landform bases its classifications; it is exported so that the TPI surfaces can be inspected, mapped, or used in other analyses.

Usage

tpi(
  x,
  scale = 3,
  units = c("cells", "map"),
  shape = c("square", "circle", "annulus"),
  inner = NULL,
  centre = FALSE,
  std = c("global", "local", "none")
)

Arguments

x

A single-layer SpatRaster (or a RasterLayer, which is converted internally) representing elevation.

scale

Size of the neighbourhood. If units = "cells" (default), the width of the moving window in cells (an odd integer >= 3; e.g. 3 gives a 3 x 3 window). If units = "map", the radius of the neighbourhood (or the half-width of the window, for shape = "square") in map units; for longitude/latitude rasters, map units are metres.

units

Either "cells" (default) or "map"; see scale.

shape

Shape of the neighbourhood: "square" (default), "circle", or "annulus" (a ring; requires inner).

inner

Inner radius of the annulus, in the same units as scale (for units = "cells", a radius in cells). Ignored unless shape = "annulus".

centre

Logical. Should the focal cell be included when computing the neighbourhood mean (and standard deviation)? Default FALSE, in line with the definition of TPI as the difference between a cell and its surroundings. See Details.

std

Standardisation: "global" (default), "local", or "none". See Details.

Value

A single-layer SpatRaster with the (standardised) TPI.

Details

Standardisation. With std = "global" the TPI is converted to z-scores using the mean and standard deviation of the TPI over the whole raster, so that values express the number of standard deviations from the grid mean. This is the standardisation used by Weiss (2001) and in Jenness's TPI extension (Jenness 2006), to which the classification thresholds in landform refer.
With std = "local" the TPI of each cell is divided by the standard deviation of elevation within its own neighbourhood. This is the "deviation from mean elevation" (DEV) of Wilson and Gallant (2000), which De Reu et al. (2013) found preferable in landscapes whose relief varies strongly from place to place. Be aware that, in nearly flat areas, the local standard deviation is very small, so that minimal elevation noise is magnified into large standardised values; on perfectly flat areas the local standardisation is undefined (NA). This was the (only) standardisation used by landform up to version 0.2.
With std = "none" the raw TPI (in elevation units) is returned.

Focal cell. With std = "global", including or excluding the focal cell rescales every TPI value by the same constant (n-1)/n, which cancels out in the z-scores; the choice therefore only affects cells close to the raster edges or to NA cells, where the neighbourhood is incomplete. It matters with std = "local" and std = "none".

Edges. Cells beyond the raster boundary, and NA cells, are ignored when averaging; TPI near edges is therefore computed from an incomplete neighbourhood.

Map units for longitude/latitude rasters. Cell sizes in metres are approximated at the latitude of the centre of the raster; over large latitudinal extents the neighbourhood is therefore only approximately constant in ground size.

References

De Reu, J., Bourgeois, J., Bats, M., Zwertvaegher, A., Gelorini, V., De Smedt, P., Chu, W., Antrop, M., De Maeyer, P., Finke, P., Van Meirvenne, M., Verniers, J. and Crombé, P. (2013). Application of the topographic position index to heterogeneous landscapes. Geomorphology, 186, 39-49.

Guisan, A., Weiss, S. B. and Weiss, A. D. (1999). GLM versus CCA spatial modeling of plant species distribution. Plant Ecology, 143, 107-122.

Jenness, J. (2006). Topographic Position Index (tpi_jen.avx) extension for ArcView 3.x, v. 1.2. Jenness Enterprises.

Weiss, A. (2001). Topographic Position and Landforms Analysis. Poster presentation, ESRI User Conference, San Diego, CA.

Wilson, J. P. and Gallant, J. C. (eds) (2000). Terrain Analysis: Principles and Applications. Wiley, New York.

See also

landform, focal

Examples

dem <- malta_dtm()

# standardised TPI, 9 x 9 cell window (360 m at 40 m resolution)
t9 <- tpi(dem, scale = 9)
terra::plot(t9, main = "Standardised TPI (9 x 9 cells)")


# raw TPI over a 500 m circular neighbourhood
t500 <- tpi(dem, scale = 500, units = "map", shape = "circle", std = "none")
terra::plot(t500, main = "TPI (m), 500 m radius")
